verses.text: For the music director. A psalm for reflection by the sons of Korah. Like a deer panting for streams of water, my soul longs for you, God.
My soul thirsts for God, the living God. When can I come and stand before him?
My tears have been my food day and night, while people keep asking, “Where is your God?”
I pour out my soul as I remember how I walked with the crowd and led them to God’s house, a festival crowd shouting for joy and singing praise.
Why are you so downcast, my soul? Why are you so restless inside me? Put your hope in God. I’ll praise him again for the rescue his presence brings.
My God, my soul is downcast within me. So I remember you from the land of the Jordan, from the heights of Hermon, and from Mount Mizar.
Deep calls to deep in the roar of your waterfalls. All your waves and surges have swept over me.
By day the LORD sends his faithful love. At night his song stays with me, a prayer to the God of my life.
I say to God, my rock, “Why have you forgotten me? Why do I go around grieving under my enemy’s oppression?”
My enemies’ taunts cut like a sword in my bones. They keep asking me, “Where is your God?”
Why are you so downcast, my soul? Why are you so restless inside me? Put your hope in God. I’ll praise him again, my Savior and my God.
